newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia pledges crackdown on copyright violation.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia pledges crackdown on copyright violation.

text.p: Indonesia has pledged to pursue a crackdown on intellectual property rights violations, including music cassette piracy, a senior cabinet minister said on Friday.

"We must uphold the law. We will combat those copyright violations, including the cassette piracy," State Secretary Murdiono told reporters after meeting Arpad Bogsch, the director general of the World Intellectual Property Organisation.
"We will continue to improve our laws on intellectual property right issues."
The United States on April 30 cited a number of countries, including Indonesia, where it said copyright violations were rampant.
Indonesia's parliament on March 22 passed amendments to laws aimed at strengthening protection of intellectual property rights.
Murdiono said at the time that people convicted of pirating software faced a maximum penalty of seven years imprisonment and a fine of 100 million rupiah (about $41,000).
He had also said displaying, circulating and selling pirated goods could be punished by five years in jail and a fine of 50 million rupiah.
